newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks seen burdened by currency woes.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks seen burdened by currency woes.

text.p: Philippine stocks slumped on Friday to a 21-month low and analysts said the market could drop further next week on investor concerns over the region's currency woes.
The main index tumbled for the seventh straight session by 44.56 points, or 1.79 percent, to close at 2,448.93 points.
The market barometer fell through the 2,500 support level and has shed 22.37 percent from 3,154.48 at the start of the year.
Shares were hit by renewed weakness in the peso as the Indonesian rupiah, which reached new lows against the dollar in early trade, triggered fresh sales of other Asian currencies.
Brokers said a technical fault at the Philippine stock exchange, which halted trading for more than an hour, also dampened sentiment.

"The market fell as we see currency concerns undermining confidence. The volatility should continue and support may be at 2,200 to 2,300," said Louie Bate, managing director for equities at ING Baring Securities.

Foreign funds would continue to get out of Asian markets and local share prices would test previous lows in the coming weeks, said a HSBC James Capel Securities Phils analyst who asked not to be identified.
If the market holds at the projected support level, an initial resistance of 2,550 may be tested, one trader said.
But most brokers believed any rally in the near-term would be technical in nature due to shares reaching oversold status.

"There may be a one-day rally but really no strong recovery. We think there's even going to be a sharp drop next week still on the currency situation. We may venture into unchartered territory," said Orion-Squire Capital research head Cilette Liboro.
